ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every shareholder, director, authorized signatory, and ultimate beneficial owner must be screened before SAMR filing against the OFAC SDN List and non-SDN sanctions lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK Treasury Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, PRC Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Foreign Affairs sanctions and counter-entity lists, and the PBOC domestic PEP database. A positive PEP match requires independent source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; any sanctions match is an automatic stop event. The WFOE must also verify that UberEats and DoorDash payout rails are not routed through a sanctioned bank, jurisdiction, or digital-asset intermediary, and must document negative adverse-media findings for all UBOs for seven years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) / SAMR Enterprise Name Self-service Check and Registration System operated by the State Administration for Market Regulation at provincial and city market supervision bureaus
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE's Chinese legal name must be registered in simplified Chinese characters and must follow a four-tier structure: administrative division + distinctive enterprise name + industry description + organizational form (limited liability company). The English name is optional but, if used, must be filed with the tax and customs authority and must correspond phonetically or semantically to the Chinese name. Pinyin transliterations are permitted when the investor name contains non-Latin characters or when coining a phonetic distinctive element from a foreign brand. The registry requires that the distinctive segment not be identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names in the same industry and administrative district; homophone protection applies to characters with the same pinyin and similar shape.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: China or Chinese when implying national-level sponsorship
Bank, Securities, Insurance, Trust, Fund, Futures, Exchange, Clearing
Group, Holding, International when not supported by qualifying status or approval
Military, Police, Communist Party, Red Cross, Emblem, Flag, Anthem-related terms
Chinese characters and pinyin strings that match a registered trademark of a third party without consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR rejects the proposed WFOE name, the applicant has 15 working days from the written rejection to file an administrative appeal with the rejecting market supervision bureau. The appeal must set out the legal basis for registrability, demonstrate distinctiveness and non-conflict with senior rights, and attach a certified comparison against the NECIPS database. A notarized power of attorney and legalized identity documents of the Hong Kong shareholder must accompany the appeal. If the bureau sustains the rejection, the applicant may apply for administrative reconsideration to the next higher SAMR authority within 60 days, and thereafter bring an administrative lawsuit in the people's court within 6 months from the reconsideration decision or statutory silence.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office, postal-only commercial mailbox, or digital address is rejected by the SAMR for a WFOE operating a ghost kitchen. The registered address must be a fixed physical premises within the municipal scope of the registration authority; it must be identifiable, contain a functional office or management workstation, and be able to receive summons and regulatory correspondence. Local tax bureaus reject virtual offices for VAT control because the entity must match the food business license production site and issue VAT invoices from a physical equipment location. Banks in mainland China will refuse account opening where the registered address is only a virtual office because tripartite monitoring and local counter-inspection requirements cannot be satisfied. Shared-workspace addresses may be accepted only in certain Pilot Free Trade Zones, but food-service WFOEs benefiting from ghost kitchen delivery are not safe; a lease covering the actual cloud kitchen and an attached supervision-accessible management office is mandatory.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced inspection checklist: (1) original lease, (2) Food Business License (FBL) displayed, (3) fire safety certificate and evacuation plan, (4) kitchen personnel with health certificates, (5) separate office area with statutory books and accounting vouchers, (6) delivery platform contract and order records, (7) invoices and cash register receipts, (8) wastewater and kitchen-oil disposal contract, (9) customs and import records if any ingredients are sourced from abroad. Quantified risk: 65 to 80 percent probability of at least one unannounced SAMR or municipal market-supervision inspection within the first twelve months, and 40 percent for a joint tax-and-market-supervision visit, due to the high volatility and food-safety sensitivity of delivery-only cloud kitchens.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), Laws of Hong Kong, ss. 67, 91, 101, 112, 116, 129 and 151; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), s. 6; Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X). Hong Kong law permits a private company to be wholly foreign-owned; it is constituted as a company limited by shares, not under any separate WFOE statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, 14/F, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong; online via e-Registry (https://www.eregistry.gov.hk).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Form NNC1 (Incorporation Form for Company Limited by Shares) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is required. A Hong Kong private company limited by shares may be incorporated with one or more shares; the subscriber may pay share capital in cash or kind as stated in the statement of capital. There is no blocked escrow account requirement or statutory capital deposit under Hong Kong law. The Company will issue shares as fully paid and file a return of allotment where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] LIMITED (THE COMPANY) (Incorporated on [date] under Certificate of Incorporation No. [number] issued by the Companies Registry of Hong Kong). At the first meeting of the board of directors of the Company duly convened on [date] at [time] at the registered office, the following directors were present: [Director 1], [Director 2] and [Director 3] (if appointed). The chairperson confirmed that the meeting was properly constituted under the Articles of Association and the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622). The company secretary recorded the agenda and minutes. RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY, as follows: 1. The Board ratified the Memorandum and Articles of Association and the statement of capital contained in Incorporation Form NNC1. 2. Share Capital Subscription and Allotment. The Board approved the subscription and allotment of [number] ordinary shares of HK$[par value] each, credited as fully paid, to the subscriber shareholder(s) named in the statement of capital. No escrow or mandatory capital payment is required under Hong Kong law. The Board directed the company secretary to enter the allotment in the register of members and to issue share certificates within two months after allotment. 3. Registered Office. The Board adopted [full address in Hong Kong] as the registered office of the Company for service of documents and statutory notices. The company secretary was directed to file any change of registered office in accordance with the Companies Ordinance and to keep the address current. 4. Bank Mandate. The Board authorized the Company to open and operate bank accounts with [bank name]. [Authorized Person A] and [Authorized Person B] are appointed authorized signatories, with any two to sign together. The mandate covers operating accounts, payouts from UberEats and DoorDash, merchant acquiring accounts, loans, overdrafts, cheques, electronic transfers, and negotiable instruments. The signatures remain in force until written revocation is filed with the bank. 5. Statutory Officers. The Board appointed [Name] as director, [Name] as company secretary, [Name] as compliance officer, and [Name] as food safety manager. Each officer accepted office and agreed to act within the scope of the Ordinance. The company secretary is directed to maintain statutory registers, file annual returns, and prepare minutes. 6. Licence Authorization. The Board directed management to file for the Business Registration Certificate, Food Business Registration or Food Factory Licence, and any environmental or fire clearances prior to commencement of operations. The Chief Executive Officer and company secretary are jointly authorized to execute all applications, indemnities, and undertakings. The resolutions under items 1 through 6 are effective immediately and shall be recorded by the company secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Search and Submission of Incorporation Form NNC1
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry e-Registry online portal and Cyber Search Centre (https://www.isa.gov.hk/cybersearch)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search in English and optional Chinese through the Cyber Search Centre to confirm no identical or conflicting corporate name is on the Companies Register. Complete Incorporation Form NNC1 for a company limited by shares, stating the intended subscribed capital, number of shares, registered office address in Hong Kong, particulars of each shareholder, director, and company secretary, and the address within Hong Kong of the company secretary if not a body corporate. Select the correct incorporation route on e-Registry, upload the signed Articles of Association, pay the prescribed registration fee, and submit. The Registry examines the statutory declarations. If the application is complete, issue the Certificate of Incorporation. For a delivery-only cloud kitchen, state the principal business purpose as delivery-only multi-brand cloud kitchen facility operations so that the company registry records match the FEHD licence application.
required_dossiers: Form NNC1
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notice to Business Registration Office and Application for Business Registration if not using integrated e-Registry
Copy of proposed registered office address
Identity documents of shareholders, directors and company secretary
Consent to act as director and company secretary declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry raises a requisition or query, the applicant shall respond through e-Registry within 14 days by amending the NNC1 and re-uploading the corrected documents. If the name is refused, select a new name and file a fresh application; any overpayment should be refunded on request, and resubmission must include the corrected statutory declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the Inland Revenue Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Business Registration Office, 15/F, Revenue Tower, 5 Gloucester Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of incorporation, ensure the Company has a Business Registration Certificate. If the certificate was not issued together with the Certificate of Incorporation, file an application with the Business Registration Office using the integrated electronic system or Form IRBR 1, and pay the prescribed business registration fee and levy. The application must give the company's name, address, nature of business, date of commencement, and details of any branch. For the ghost kitchen, the business nature should be typed as delivery-only cloud kitchen serving online meal platforms, and the principal place of business must match the FEHD licence address. Update the certificate on any change of particulars within one month. Display the certificate at the registered office and each branch. The certificate is separate from the food business licence and does not authorize food operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Form IRBR 1 where not integrated
Principal place of business address proof such as tenancy agreement
Identity document of company signatory
Business nature and commencement date statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If processing is delayed, attend the Business Registration Office with supporting documents. If a penalty is imposed for late business registration, submit a letter of reasonable excuse citing first-time incorporation and non-commencement of trade, and apply for penalty remission under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Constitutional Documents, and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Company Secretary; Hong Kong Monetary Authority-regulated licensed banks for corporate account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting in Hong Kong by electronic or physical attendance in accordance with the Articles. Adopt the formal Pro-Forma First Board Resolution approving and ratifying the share allotment, adoption of registered office, appointment of directors, company secretary, and authorized bank signatories, and the instruction to open operating and merchant accounts. After the meeting, the company secretary shall prepare the resolution minutes, issue share certificates, and open the statutory registers of members, directors, company secretary, and charges. The board authorizes the finance director to submit account opening KYC documents to the chosen licensed bank and to connect payment rails with UberEats Payout and DoorDash Payout. For a Hong Kong private company, the company secretary must normally be an individual resident in Hong Kong or a body corporate with a registered office in Hong Kong.
required_dossiers: Signed board meeting minutes implementing the pro-forma resolution
Certificate of Incorporation
Business Registration Certificate
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Director and shareholder identification and address proof
Beneficial ownership statement for bank KYC
Fit and proper declarations for directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines account opening, obtain a written reason, supplement the corporate structure chart and source-of-funds evidence, and resubmit to the bank's compliance unit or another licensed bank. If the Companies Registry queries statutory register formats, amend within 14 days and request an extension before any late filing fee accrues.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Food Business Registration or Food Factory Licence Application to FEHD
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD), Food Business Licensing and District Environmental Hygiene Offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before beginning any commercial cooking, apply for the appropriate FEHD licence. For a delivery-only virtual brand kitchen that prepares and delivers food to consumers through digital platforms, the operator should apply for a Food Business Registration for a delivery-only restaurant, or a Food Factory Licence if the kitchen operates as a central production unit supplying multiple virtual brands. Prepare a scaled floor plan showing the kitchen layout, equipment, wash-up sinks, grease traps, storage areas, toilets, ventilation systems, and refuse storage. Obtain the landlord's consent and certificate from the building owner if subdivision or structural changes are involved. Submit the completed application, business registration certificate, tenancy agreement, floor plans, and fire safety documents. Pay the licence fee and await FEHD inspection. The licence must be displayed at the premises before food activities are conducted.
required_dossiers: FEHD licence application form
Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration Certificate
Lease and landlord's consent
Scaled floor plan and drainage plan
Certificate of Fire Service Installations and Equipment
Waste disposal arrangement contract with licensed collector
Food safety management plan based on HACCP principles
Proposed menu and virtual brand list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried due to layout or ventilation deficiencies, engage a licensed architect or engineer to amend the floor plan and resubmit. If FEHD refuses the licence, the applicant may request a written statement of reasons and submit a fresh application with corrected plans, or appeal to the Municipal Services Appeals Board within the time prescribed by the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental, Fire, and Occupational Clearances Prior to Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Environmental Protection Department (EPD); Fire Services Department (FSD); Buildings Department (BD); Labour Department Occupational Safety and Health Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the kitchen's environmental obligations. If the kitchen will discharge trade effluent, obtain any Effluent Discharge Licence from the EPD under the Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358) or keep evidence of exemption for domestic-only discharge. Since used cooking oil is a chemical waste, register as a chemical waste producer with the EPD and retain a contract with a licensed waste collector. Apply for the Fire Services Department certificate for the fire service installation, including kitchen exhaust systems, wet or dry chemical suppression systems, fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, and means of escape. For the structural load of any mezzanines or equipment platforms, obtain a report from a registered structural engineer acceptable to the Buildings Department. Arrange occupational safety training and first aid facilities through Labour Department approved providers. Do not begin operations until the final safety and environmental approvals are in place.
required_dossiers: EPD chemical waste producer registration form
Effluent Discharge Licence application or exemption letter
Grease trap and drainage maintenance contract
Fire service installation completion certificate
FSD building fire safety inspection report
Structural engineer's report on floors and platforms
Labour Department safety training certificates
Facility emergency response plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If EPD or FSD identifies non-compliance, remediate the defects in writing within 14 days, obtain a re-inspection, and keep a compliance log. If an Effluent Discharge Licence is refused for effluent quality reasons, install additional pre-treatment and resubmit; if the fire certificate is suspended, stop the affected kitchen line until the Fire Services Department re-certifies the installations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Food and Environmental Hygiene Department (FEHD); Environmental Protection Department (EPD); Fire Services Department (FSD); Buildings Department (BD); Labour Department Occupational Safety and Health Branch
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Food Business Registration for a delivery-only restaurant or Food Factory Licence for a multi-brand central kitchen, issued under the Food Business Regulation (Cap. 132X) and the Food Safety Ordinance (Cap. 612); Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) is also required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department, Hong Kong SAR Government (EPD)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment report under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499) for a standard delivery-only

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; taxpayer-facing services are conducted via provincial portals of the China Electronic Tax Bureau, accessible through the official STA website at www.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The CN WFOE is a Chinese resident enterprise and therefore its statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) is the 18-character Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) printed on its Business License issued by the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). There is no separate TIN registration certificate. The mandatory procedure is as follows: (1) incorporate the WFOE with the provincial SAMR and obtain the Business License; (2) tax registration is automatically completed through the 'one license, one code' information-sharing mechanism between SAMR and the tax authority, with the USCC serving as the enterprise tax ID; (3) within 30 days of license issuance, the entity must log in to the China Electronic Tax Bureau to complete post-registration verification, confirm the taxpayer type, register the legal representative's credentials, and set up VAT invoice quota; (4) if the WFOE will directly export goods or services, it must separately obtain a customs registration code via the International Trade Single Window and complete the foreign trade operator filing with the local commerce authority; (5) where the Hong Kong parent (an offshore non-resident enterprise) derives China-source income from the WFOE, it may apply for non-resident enterprise tax registration through a withholding agent and submit a Hong Kong tax residency certificate to claim benefits under the Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA); (6) the WFOE should also register its payroll and social insurance arisings through the administrative human resources and social security platform for withholding income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The People's Republic of China does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election regime for entity classification. The WFOE is mandatorily treated as a Chinese tax-resident enterprise under the Enterprise Income Tax Law and is subject to entity-level corporate income tax on its worldwide income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Provisional Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Value Added Tax, superseded by the VAT Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2026)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no economic turnover threshold for basic VAT registration; any entity holding a business license must complete tax registration within 30 days. However, annual taxable turnover exceeding RMB 5,000,000 triggers mandatory registration as a General VAT Taxpayer, requiring standard VAT rates to be charged and input VAT to be creditable. Enterprises with annual turnover not exceeding RMB 5,000,000 may remain Small-Scale VAT Taxpayers and pay VAT at the statutory levy rate (currently 3% or 1% where applicable), with monthly sales up to RMB 100,000 exempt from VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates a mandatory nationwide electronic invoicing and fiscal clearance system under the Golden Tax Phase IV infrastructure. VAT invoices must be issued via the China Electronic Tax Bureau's Fully Digital Electronic Invoice (FDEI) platform, either through the government-furnished free invoicing software or compliant API integrations. Every invoice is transmitted in real time to the central tax database, assigned a unique 20-digit invoice number and an anti-counterfeit QR code, and subjected to automatic risk control and audit-matching. There is no separate fiscal stamping; instead, the FDEI platform performs instantaneous tax-control validation and invoice status verification. The system supports fully digital e-invoices and eliminates paper invoice requirements, while special VAT invoices used for input deduction must be uploaded to the VAT Invoice Comprehensive Service Platform for authentication.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the PRC VAT Law and the Administrative Measures for the Refund (Exemption) of VAT on Export Goods and Services, zero-rating is available for (a) goods that are exported from China and legally cleared by customs, and (b) a narrow list of cross-border services supplied to non-resident enterprises and wholly consumed outside China, including certain offshore information technology, licencing and consulting services. The ghost kitchen's underlying onshore catering and food-delivery services are subject to VAT at 6% and are not zero-rated. If the operator exports packaged food products as goods, the sale of goods qualifies for zero-rating upon proper customs clearance. Commission income earned from offshore delivery platforms such as UberEats or DoorDash may potentially qualify as zero-rated cross-border information technology services if the service is rendered to an overseas enterprise, the consideration is received in foreign currency, and the service is not used or consumed within China, but the burden of proof is on the taxpayer and the tax authorities scrutinise such claims strictly.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Export Entry) with customs registration number
Bill of Lading (ocean or air waybill) issued by a licensed carrier evidencing physical shipment for goods exports
Foreign Exchange Income Declaration Form (bank receipt voucher showing inward remittance of convertible foreign currency)
Commercial Invoice in the name of the offshore buyer
Export Sales Contract or Purchase Order
VAT Special Invoice for the exported goods where input VAT refund is claimed
Export Tax Refund (Exemption) Application Form submitted via the Electronic Tax Bureau
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is verified through electronic cross-matching of customs declaration data, foreign exchange receipt data and VAT invoice data under the Golden Tax Phase IV system. Any mismatch or missing document results in an unqualified export declaration and the tax authority will typically suspend or deny the refund. If the exporter fails to repatriate foreign exchange within the statutory 180-day period or submits false declarations, the tax authority will retroactively claw back the zero-rated refund, impose a daily overdue surcharge of 0.05% on the unpaid tax, and levy a fine of 50% to 500% of the tax amount involved under Article 63 of the Law on Tax Collection and Administration. In cases involving fraudulent export tax refunds, criminal liability arises under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, with penalties ranging from fixed-term imprisonment to life imprisonment, plus confiscation of property.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and its State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China operates a strictly managed and partially convertible currency regime. Renminbi is convertible on current account transactions for qualified enterprise flows after the bank performs verifiable authenticity checks, but capital account transactions remain subject to SAFE registration, approval or quota mechanisms. For a Hong Kong-invested WFOE operating ISIC 5610 ghost kitchens, local RMB collections from delivery platforms do not require separate SAFE approval, but any use of funds abroad and any repatriation of profits to Hong Kong require documentation. Dividends are treated as current account remittances only after the WFOE completes annual statutory audit under Chinese GAAP, files its corporate income tax returns, approves the profit-distribution resolution, and withholds 10% dividend tax subject to possible reduction to 5% if the Hong Kong parent qualifies as a beneficial owner under the Mainland/Hong Kong Double Tax Arrangement. Capital contributions from HK must be recorded via SAFE's Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration, received in the designated foreign exchange capital account at a SAFE-designated bank, and settled into RMB after authenticity verification. There is no mandatory surrender ratio for export proceeds at collection date; enterprises may retain 100% of foreign exchange earnings in current accounts, but receipts must be repatriated and reconciled with customs declarations and trade monitoring under the ASOne system. The principal hurdle for profit remittance is a bank's demand for accounting reports, tax payment proof, and evidence that undistributed prior-year losses are fully offset.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For goods-trade export receipts, the PRC has adopted a repatriation with provisional reporting rule rather than forced conversion. The exporter must repatriate export proceeds through a designated bank within 180 days from the date of customs export declaration unless SAFE has approved an extension for receivables financing or long-lived supply chains. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero; however, 100% of the export proceeds may be retained in a foreign exchange current account or settled into RMB at the client's discretion, and any balance retained beyond the bank's prescribed limit must be flagged to SAFE through the trade monitoring system. On conversion, the exporter provides the customs declaration, export invoice, packing list and transaction code in the bank's ASOne interface.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Dedicated SAFE FDI Capital Settlement Account plus CNY Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Multi-currency current account for operating foreign exchange and payroll settlement
CNY Basic Operations Account with secondary export proceeds receivable subledger
RMB Basic Deposit Account and foreign exchange current account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability Rating: Low (not legally feasible). Under PBOC and SAFE licensing rules, only domestically licensed commercial banks and approved payment institutions may hold and clear RMB and foreign currency for legal entities in China. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Revolut Business, Currenxie or Airwallex, unless they hold a mainland payment license, cannot open accounts for the WFOE or execute in-country FX settlements; their use as an account provider would constitute unauthorized cross-border financial business. The WFOE may use licensed fintech platforms only for connectivity or treasury dashboards, but every settlement of funds still passes through the Tier-1 Chinese clearing bank connected to the ASOne FX verification system.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical in-branch presence is mandatory for at least one person authorized as the operator. Under PBOC's Corporate Bank Account Management Measures and AML/CDD rules, the statutory representative must appear in person with the original business licence and passport/ID for account opening, or the statutory representative may appoint a mainland-based manager through a notarized power of attorney in both Chinese and English, plus the WFOE's chop/seal registration record. Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted by Tier-1 banks for a newly established WFOE; some banks permit video KYC only after the physical interview has been completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A newly constructed Hong Kong-owned WFOE with no domestic banking history injects shareholder capital through a Hong Kong bank within the first 90 days of incorporation, raising suspicion of unlawful money passing or circular capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the SAFE Foreign Direct Investment registration certificate, the notarized shareholder capital subscription schedule from the Hong Kong board, shareholder resolution on investment, bank-to-bank SWIFT MT103 receipt, HK parent bank statement and audited financial statements, plus an International Certificate of Incumbency and Companies Registry current extract identifying the ultimate beneficial owner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Delivery-only ghost kitchen model creates a customer-not-present profile with high-volume aggregated settlement from a small number of marketplace payouts, undermining the traditional invoice-per-transaction audit trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit executed UberEats and DoorDash merchant agreements, payout settlement reports from each marketplace for the first six months, a reconciliation ledger linking gross food sales to net payouts, effective food operational licenses, and a written operational flowchart demonstrating that each settlement corresponds to verified customer orders.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient physical substance at the dark kitchen site, because there is no customer-facing storefront and the bank suspects that the premises may be unoccupied or sublet without authorization.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the notarized lease for the ghost kitchen facility, the food business licence and fire safety acceptance certificate, staffing contracts and payroll records, daily production logs, a cloud kitchen platform certification, and a bank compliance requested video walk-through of the facility.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity because the Hong Kong parent uses nominee shareholders or trust arrangements and the bank cannot establish whether any bearer instruments exist.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a validated beneficial ownership register identifying all natural persons with more than 5% control, signed trust deeds and nominee removal declarations, official confirmation from the Hong Kong Companies Registry that no bearer shares are outstanding, passport copies of all UBOs, and a legal opinion confirming the absence of bearer instruments and the reliability of the ownership chain.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity injections from the Hong Kong parent shall be transmitted via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 into the SAFE-registered FDI capital account at the designated Chinese bank. The remittance must carry the standardized SAFE purpose code for foreign direct investment paid-in capital, the SAFE FDI registration number, and the exact WFOE legal name in both Chinese and English. The receiving bank will screen the routing against the FDI registration, conduct a funds-origin check, settle the foreign exchange into RMB using the onshore spot rate, and record the transaction in the ASOne system. After settlement, a certified public accountant issues a capital verification report confirming that the contribution has been paid in accordance with the registered nominal timetable; the company seal register must evidence the respective board approval and the enterprise must keep the verification report for subsequent dividend repatriation and tax filings.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements include SWIFT MT103 for high-value open account payments to overseas suppliers, commercial letters of credit at sight or usance for structural procurement financing of kitchen equipment and packaging, and documentary collections for intra-group supplies requiring proof of delivery before payment. All outbound remittances require authentic underlying documents such as purchase contracts, commercial invoices, packing lists, customs declarations and the SAFE payment purpose code. The WFOE must also comply with SAFE's trade monitoring data reporting and, if outbound payments involve Hong Kong parent balances, ensure the transaction is supported by the intercompany agreement and transfer pricing file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore delivered CNY forward contracts with a SAFE-licensed Chinese bank, permissible only for real current account receipts and payments with full trade documentation and physical settlement at maturity

Cross-currency CNY/HKD or CNY/USD swaps permissible for long-term FDI exposure after SAFE registration, required to be linked to outstanding registered FDI capital or foreign debt and cannot be terminated on a purely notional basis

Offshore NDF contracts are prohibited for the mainland WFOE to book directly; the Chinese bank cannot issue onshore NDF for CNY settlement purposes, and any NDF hedging for the Hong Kong parent must be executed outside mainland China by the HK entity under Hong Kong regulatory boundaries

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a Private Company (Form NAR1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry, Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation of the Hong Kong private limited company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing escalates by age of delinquency: HK$870 after 3 months, HK$1,740 after 6 months, HK$2,610 after 9 months, and HK$3,480 after 12 months; persistent failure exposes the company and each responsible officer to prosecution, fine and daily default fine, and ultimately administrative strike-off under Cap. 622.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry of the current one-year Business Registration Certificate; the IRD issues a renewal notice before the expiry date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts a late-payment penalty under the Business Registration Ordinance and possible summary prosecution with a maximum fine of HK$5,000; continued failure may render the business unregistered and subject the company and responsible officers to additional fines, penalties, and compulsory strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) with audited financial statements, tax computation, and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within one month from the date of issue of the BIR51 return, with the IRD normally issuing corporation returns in April/May for a 31 December year-end; extension may be applied for through an authorized tax representative
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-filing permits the Inland Revenue Department to issue estimated assessments, impose monetary penalties up to HK$10,000, and add additional tax of up to three times the amount of tax undercharged; continued default may lead to prosecution under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return (Form BIR56A and individual BIR56B forms) for all employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the issue of the annual BIR56A return pack; for the year of assessment ending 31 March the pack is generally issued in April and is due on or before 1 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file an Employer's Return may result in penalties up to HK$10,000 per offense and additional tax of up to three times the tax undercharged; responsible officers may be prosecuted and personally liable.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every Hong Kong private limited company must appoint a certified public accountant holding a practising certificate as auditor and produce audited financial statements for each financial year unless it qualifies as a small private company or small group. A private company qualifies for audit exemption for a financial year if it satisfies at least two of the following three conditions and no member requires an audit: (i) annual revenue does not exceed HK$100 million; (ii) total assets do not exceed HK$100 million; (iii) number of employees does not exceed 100. If the Hong Kong WFOE entity exceeds any two of these thresholds, belongs to a group that cannot qualify as a small group, is in a regulated sector such as banking, insurance, securities, or licensed financial services, or applicable shareholders require an audit, an independent certified public accountant audit is legally mandatory and cannot be waived.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) as issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants, being substantially converged with IFRS; eligible small private companies may apply HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS for Private Entities / SME Reporting Standard) and simplified financial reporting and disclosure requirements under the Companies Ordinance provisions on altered financial reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not maintain a public annual UBO filing. However, under Cap. 622 Part 17A each company must maintain a Register of Significant Controllers at its registered office and update any change in a significant controller's details or any shareholding transfer within 7 calendar days. The Companies Registry Annual Return (Form NAR1) is required within 42 days after the incorporation anniversary and must present the current members and shareholding structure. Any share transfer instrument must be submitted to the Stamp Office for ad valorem stamp duty payment within 30 days of execution. Changes of directors, company secretary, or registered office are filed through the prescribed Companies Registry forms within 15 days of the relevant change. Failure to maintain or update the Significant Controllers Register is an offence carrying a fine of up to HK$25,000 and a daily default fine of HK$700; persistent default can contribute to prosecution and administrative strike-off proceedings.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D expenses super deduction at 100% of qualifying R&D costs; Small Low-Profit Enterprise preferential rate (5% effective on taxable income up to RMB 3 million subject to eligibility); other incentives may apply for encouraged industries.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 – Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (A-Type) and associated schedules; filed electronically via the official online tax filing system of the State Taxation Administration (STA)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional returns plus annual final settlement
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly filings due within 15 days after each calendar quarter-end; annual final return due by May 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Revenue (营业收入) – total revenue derived from sales of goods or services, including online food delivery platform sales.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all revenue from P.R. China operations. If transactions with Hong Kong affiliates are underpriced, impose arm's-length adjustments. Include conversion of foreign currency at prevailing exchange rates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating Costs (营业成本) – costs directly attributable to generating operating revenue, including raw materials, kitchen rental, platform commissions and delivery logistics.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure transfer pricing policies for procurement from related parties are documented. Apportion platform commission costs accurately; no deduction for illegal kickbacks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and Surcharges (税金及附加) – urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, real estate taxes, stamp duties, and other tax-like charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only such levies that are computed on current-period taxable turnover; not the enterprise income tax itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling Expenses (销售费用) – marketing, advertising, promotional discounts, rider subsidies and brand-building expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify business genuineness; related-party marketing fees to HK parent must be supported by service arrangements and benefit tests.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative Expenses (管理费用) – management fees, depreciation, staff wages relating to administration, and office overheads.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a HK headquarters allocates management fees, the WFOE must substantiate the economic benefit, include supporting agreements, and apply arm's-length rate; otherwise disallowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial Expenses (财务费用) – interest expense on borrowings, exchange gains/losses (net), and bank charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to Hong Kong lenders: deduct only if the underlying loan is at arm's length and properly documented; thinly capitalized rules under EIT Law Article 46 may cap deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total Profit (利润总额) – accounting profit derived after operating profit plus non-operating income less non-operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Serves as starting point for tax adjustments bridging accounting profit to taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable Income (应纳税所得额) – accounting profit adjusted for permanent and temporary differences, including transfer pricing adjustments and disallowed expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include mandatory adjustments like excess entertainment expenses (deductible up to 60% but capped at 0.5% of revenue), and R&D super deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax Payable (应纳所得税额) – taxable income multiplied by 25% statutory rate, reduced by preferential rates and foreign tax credit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholder dividends are not deducted here; they give rise to withholding tax when distributed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual Tax Payable (实际应纳所得税额) – tax payable after credit for quarterly prepayments, tax credits, and special tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any overpayment can be refunded or offset; underpayment triggers interest and late payment surcharge.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: RMB 2,000 fine (up to RMB 10,000 for severe) under Tax Administration Law Article 62; 0.05% daily late-payment interest on unpaid tax (Article 32). Underpayment due to fraud or evasion: 50%–500% of the tax shortfall (Article 63) and possible criminal prosecution under Criminal Law Article 201.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (statutory rate for non-resident enterprises under PRC EIT Law Article 3 and Article 27)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim the 5% Mainland-Hong Kong DTA rate, the Hong Kong shareholder must be the 'beneficial owner' and directly hold at least 25% of the equity of the Chinese WFOE. Procedure: (1) Self-assess eligibility; (2) file the return with the WFOE when the dividend distribution is declared; (3) retain supporting documentation including the HK Tax Residency Certificate (TRC), audited financial statements, shareholding register, and beneficial ownership declaration as required under SAT Announcement No. 35/2019. The WFOE withholds the treaty rate after the beneficial owner provides documentation; tax authorities may requalify the application on review.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory 10% withholding; DTA-reduced to 7% generally, and 5% for interest derived from banks or financial institutions. Royalties (industrial, commercial, scientific equipment, copyrights etc.): statutory 10%; DTA-reduced to 7% if beneficial owner is HK resident.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required for related-party transactions exceeding: RMB 200 million for tangible goods transfers; RMB 100 million for financial asset transfers; RMB 100 million for intangible transfers; RMB 40 million for other related-party transactions (SAT Bulletin No. 42/2016). Master File required when aggregate annual related-party turnover exceeds RMB 1 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Under PRC law, general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) in EIT Law Art. 47 and CFC rules in Art. 45 permit the tax authorities to recharacterize entities lacking commercial substance. The Chinese WFOE must demonstrate real operational substance, including actual kitchen facilities, employees, and decision-making in China, as its place of effective management; the Hong Kong holding company also must satisfy Hong Kong Economic Substance Requirements (ESR) if it conducts relevant business (equity holding usually benefits from reduced substance tests).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE deliberately underprices sales of virtual-brand food products sold to a Hong Kong related distributor, or overpays fictitious management fees, shifting taxable profits out of China, without maintaining contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC Tax Administration Law (TAL) Article 63, this constitutes tax evasion: assessment of the underpaid tax, 0.05% daily late interest (TAL Art. 32), and a fine of 50% to 500% of the unpaid tax amount; criminal liability under Criminal Law Art. 201 for tax evasion where the amount is substantial.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve or endorse such false pricing are 'directly responsible personnel' and face criminal imprisonment (up to 7 years for major evasion) and fines; civil liability extends to restitution of the tax loss from the company's assets; may be personally joint and severally liable if the corporate veil is pierced under Company Law Art. 20 for abusive control.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax – Failure to Withhold on Outbound Dividends/Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE distributes dividends to its Hong Kong parent or pays royalties for virtual kitchen brand licensing to a Hong Kong entity but fails to withhold the 10% (or reduced DTA) WHT, or fails to obtain the TRC and beneficial-owner documents, and withholds at zero.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TAL Article 69: the tax authority will recover the deficient tax from the payee and impose a penalty on the withholding agent equal to 50% to 300% of the un-withheld tax; late-payment interest also accrues. If the failure is intentional to facilitate evasion, criminal liability may attach.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and financial officers who formally authorize the gross distribution without withholding may be subject to administrative fines and, in egregious cases, criminal liability as abettors to tax evasion under Criminal Law Art. 201; personal assets may be reachable if they caused the company's liability through willful misconduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent is a mere paper company with no office, employees, or business activity, used to artificially obtain DTA benefits (5% dividend rate) and to divert Chinese profits; the WFOE channels excessive platform fees to this shell.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under PRC EIT Law Art. 47 (GAAR), the tax authorities may re-develop the transaction to align with economic substance, increase taxable income, and assess interest plus late-payment penalties. Hong Kong ESR Act imposes fines and potential prosecution for a company that fails the economic substance test; Chinese tax authorities may deem the HK entity as having its place of effective management in China, subjecting it to 25% corporate tax on worldwide income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the WFOE and HK shell may be subject to blacklisting (exit bans), asset freezes, and personal restitution for facilitating the abusive scheme; if the arrangement is characterized as fraudulent, imprisonment for tax evasion under Criminal Law Art. 201 applies; under PRC Company Law Art. 20, shareholders abusing limited liability may face unlimited personal liability for company debts.
